title: Knowledge check: Introduction to REST API Development

questions.prompt: An API provider and consumer need a stable boundary. What belongs in the contract?
options: A promise that all requests will succeed regardless of input or permissions.
Supported operations, input/output shapes, expected errors, and access requirements.
The provider’s internal folder layout and private database password.
Only a screenshot of the current interface, with no request or response rules.
questions.answer_key: Supported operations, input/output shapes, expected errors, and access requirements.
questions.explanation: Supported operations, input/output shapes, expected errors, and access requirements. This is especially relevant to “Introduction to REST API Development” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Introduction to REST API Development”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Use a documented request/response example and check that success and failure match the provider contract.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented request/response example and check that success and failure match the provider contract.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Introduction to REST API Development”?
options: The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
The API has no clear statement of provider/consumer responsibilities or supported operations.
questions.answer_key: The API has no clear statement of provider/consumer responsibilities or supported operations.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
